Connecticut will lend first-time buyers up to $25,000 at 0%. Then it forgives 10% of it every year.

It's called Time-To-Own. CHFA runs it, and $12.3M was left as of October 26. It sits next to a CHFA first mortgage and goes toward your down payment and closing costs. No interest, no monthly payment. After 10 years you owe nothing.

The catch: sell, refinance or move out before year 10 and you repay what's left.

In Sandy Hook, a typical home sold for about $505K this fall. A 3.5% FHA down payment on that is $17,675, which Time-To-Own can cover if you qualify. Income and purchase price limits apply, so check yours with a CHFA participating lender before you shop.

Comment OWN and I'll send you the one-page eligibility checklist.

Program terms from chfa.org as of Oct 26, 2026. Funding is limited and terms can change. I'm a Realtor, not a lender, and this isn't a loan offer.
